summary: The recorded base reproduced the original ROCm contradiction from the actual imported DSA modules: is_hip=True, is_cuda=False, DUAL_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0, and every tested token count made 0 < num_tokens <= threshold false in both the standard and k-pool gates. At exact candidate commit e64beeb06331c7f098184412db14eeb07850a9c4, the imported threshold is 1024 on HIP and both production indexers use the same helper, making the gate true for positive token counts through 1024 when an alternate stream exists and capture mode is active. The candidate regression passed, and an independent adversarial boundary test plus real cross-stream GPU computation passed on gfx950. This fully resolves the original issue's stated unsatisfiable-predicate defect; it intentionally retains the pre-existing 1024 upper bound rather than following the separate historical direction of deleting token thresholds.

The candidate's own GPU test exercises the extracted decision helper and generic stream behavior, not DSA kernels; acceptance is based on independently reproducing and correcting the original source-level predicate contradiction in the actual imported modules. Token counts above 1024 remain deliberately single-stream, matching the pre-existing CUDA policy but not the threshold-removal direction of historical PRs #9405 and #14337.
